stem:
Ishaan has $21=3\times 7$ and $22=2\times 11$. He wants to decide whether $21$ and $22$ are co-prime from those prime factorisations.

Which two claims correctly settle that decision?

options.text: The factorisations share no common prime factor, so $21$ and $22$ are co-prime.
Co-prime status also covers every pair that merely ends with different digits.
Because the listed primes $3$, $7$, $2$, and $11$ are all distinct across the two factorisations, the numbers are co-prime.
Call them co-prime only because $22$ is the larger printed number.

teacher.key_rationale: Co-prime means no shared prime factors: 3×7 and 2×11 share none. Final-digit differences or size labels are not the test.
